9. Mr. Akram Hossain Amin by filing a supplementary affidavit has raised another question relating to under valuation of the suit mentioning that the plaintiff disclosed in the plaint that the capital of the partnership was Tk.1,50,000/- and the plaintiff has paid Tk.36,000/- only towards the firm's capital and there has been a profit of Tk.10,00,000/- out of the partnership business but the suit was valued at Tk.2,000/- only which is not the proper valuation of the suit and the suit being grossly undervalued is liable to be rejected in terms of Order 7 Rule 11 (b) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submission the learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Guinoss Peat (Training) Limited Vs. Md. Fazlur Rahman reported in 1992 BLD (AD) 247. Mr. Mansur Habib on the other hand invited any attention to the valuation statement as made in the plaint Annexure A where it is stated that the suit has formally been valued at Tk.1, 000/- and filed with fixed court fee or Tk.100/- with averment made in the plaint that the plaintiff shall be bound to pay necessary court fee on the profit amount of his share that may be ascertained by accounting after the final decree and the suit at this stage cannot be said to be undervalued. 

 11. With regard to under valuation of the suit I find that the prayer for rejection of the plaint was made only on the ground that the partnership firm was not properly registered and not on the ground of under valuation. In the plaint we find as averment that the suit has been formally valued at Tk.2, 000/- with the undertaking that proper court fees would be paid after the accounting. A statement that the partnership firm was established with a capital of Tk.4, 50,000/- and the plaintiff participated in the firm by payment of Tk.36,000/- and also by furnishing the land. From the plaint we also find an assertion that the partnership firm has earned a profit of Tk.40, 00,000/-. These are averments made in the plaint and the profit earned by the firm has to be assessed after accounting by a proper authority and the plaintiff has under taken to pay the adveluram court fee according to his share of profit to be assessed by the proper authority during final decree. In view of the averment made in the plaint I do not find any substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the suit is grossly undervalued. I do not therefore find any merit in this rule.
